body:
# Drákōn, spelled the way the sources wrote it
Some restorations are cosmetic. **Drákōn** is not — the marks in this name are the difference between reading the sources and guessing at them.

Every Greek dragon is a threshold made flesh: kill one and a sanctuary, a city, or a marriage becomes possible — which is why the founders of cities are all, sooner or later, dragonslayers. The Homeric Hymn to Apóllōn tells how the god, seeking a site for his oracle, found the spring at Delphoi guarded by a great she-dragon who had nursed Typhaon and ravaged the flocks.  He shot her and left her to rot in the sun — "now rot (pytheu) here upon the fruitful soil" — and the place was called Pythō, the priestess Pythia, ever after.

That is the figure this file is about — and the temple now standing at its restored name.
## At a Glance

- **Restored name:** Drákōn
- **ASCII form:** drakon
- **Meaning:** "'The one who sees clearly' (from δέρκομαι, to see)"
- **Domain of influence:** Serpent, Guardian, Vigilance
- **Pantheon:** Greek
- **Classification:** Tier 1
- **Original script:** Δράκων
- **Series:** The Restoration Files, No. 70 of 271
## The Name Before the Marks

The name is attested as **Δράκων**. On the evidence, it means "'The one who sees clearly' (from δέρκομαι, to see)".

Strip **Drákōn** to *drakon* and 2 pieces of evidence vanish:

- **a → á** — Stress mark (acute/tone): the stress position the ASCII form cannot show.
- **o → ō** — Macron marks the long vowel: the vowel length the ASCII form cannot show.

A reader who knows the marks hears the name correctly on the first try. A reader who never sees them never gets the chance.
## The Temple That Stands Now

The restored name is not a plaque; it is an address. The temple of **Drákōn** lives at [/sites/drakon/](/sites/drakon/), with its mythology in the [lore halls](/sites/drakon/lore/), its peer-reviewed record in the [Scholarly Edition](/sites/drakon/scholars/), and its place in the pattern atlas on the [patterns floor](/sites/drakon/patterns/).

The restoration preserves more than the ASCII form can say — stress, length, or a letter the Latin keyboard lost — which places it in Tier-1: mechanically verifiable, information-rich.

Every flagship temple is hand-built to the same standard: the original script displayed with its provenance, the pronunciation reconstructed phoneme by phoneme, the sources named — because a restoration you cannot audit is just a spelling with confidence.
## The Archetype at Work

A temple is also a reading of what this figure *means* — and meanings have addresses in the modern world. The [pattern atlas](/patterns/) maps **Drákōn** to the industries its archetype genuinely resonates with, each match argued, weighted, and open to challenge:

- **Cybersecurity & Digital Protection** — The unsleeping watcher at the perimeter; the guardian serpent of every firewall.
- **Gaming, Fantasy & Entertainment IP** — Every fantasy dragon is his descendant, hoard and coil included.
- **Insurance & Protection Services** — His coil is the guarding embrace around the treasure; asset protection is his posture.

The mapping is conservative on purpose: only resonances that can be argued aloud. The rest of the atlas follows the same rule, industry by industry.
## In the Sacred Texts

The Greek tradition is not a vibe; it is a library. The [Sacred Texts collection](/texts/) holds [Theogony](/texts/theogony/), [Homeric Hymns](/texts/homeric-hymns/), and [Works and Days](/texts/works-and-days/) — the primary sources the temple's scholarship is built on, free to read, cross-linked back to the names they mention. The temple is the argument; the texts are the evidence.
